## mcrl check get

Show a check monitor.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl check get <check>

Aliases:
  get, show

Show a check monitor by ID or name.

A reference that looks like an ID (11 alphanumeric characters) is looked up
as an ID first. Prefix it with "id:" or "name:" to force either.

API: GET /api/v0/monitoring/checks/<id>, GET /api/v0/monitoring/checks
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl check get backup
  mcrl check get 3Ja1bAxcdef
```

## mcrl check list

List check monitors.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl check list [flags]

Aliases:
  list, ls

List check monitors (monitors created from check reports).

API: GET /api/v0/monitoring/checks
API key permission: Read

Examples:
  mcrl check list
  mcrl check list --jq '.[].name'

Flags:
      --limit int   maximum number of check monitors (0 = all)
```

## mcrl check report

Report check monitoring results.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl check report (--host <host> --name <name> --status <status> --message <text> | -f <file>) [flags]

Report a check result for a host, creating the check monitor on first use.

-f reads a JSON or YAML array of reports in the API's format instead; they are
sent 100 at a time. The API ignores a report whose host, name and time were
already reported, or that is 6 hours or more in the future.

API: POST /api/v0/monitoring/checks/report
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  mcrl check report --host web-1 --name backup --status OK --message "backup finished"
  mcrl check report --host web-1 --name disk --status WARNING --message "/var 85%" --notification-interval 1h

Flags:
  -f, --file string                    JSON or YAML array of reports ("-" for stdin)
      --host string                    host the check belongs to (required)
      --max-check-attempts int         alert after this many consecutive non-OK reports (1-10) (default 1)
      --message string                 message (under 1024 characters)
      --name string                    check monitor name: letters, digits, - and _ (required)
      --notification-interval string   re-notify while not OK, e.g. "30m" (10m or more; default: no re-notification)
      --status string                  OK, WARNING, CRITICAL or UNKNOWN
```

## mcrl check run

Run a command and report its result as a check.

```text
Usage:
  mcrl check run --host <host> --name <name> -- <command> [args...] [flags]

Run a command and report its result as a check monitoring result.

The exit code maps to the status like Nagios plugins: 0 OK, 1 WARNING,
2 CRITICAL, anything else (or failing to start) UNKNOWN. The command's
output is passed through and its last 1024 characters become the message.

mcrl exits with the command's exit code, so it can replace the command in
cron jobs.

API: POST /api/v0/monitoring/checks/report
API key permission: Read, Write

Examples:
  # cron: report whether the backup succeeded
  mcrl check run --host "$(hostname)" --name backup -- /usr/local/bin/backup.sh

  # run an existing check plugin
  mcrl check run --host web-1 --name http -- check-http -u https://example.com/

Flags:
      --host string                    host the check belongs to (required)
      --max-check-attempts int         alert after this many consecutive non-OK reports (1-10) (default 1)
      --name string                    check monitor name: letters, digits, - and _ (required)
      --notification-interval string   re-notify while not OK, e.g. "30m" (10m or more; default: no re-notification)
```
